             Rules of Conduct for Planning Commission Meetings
PROCEDURE FOR PUBLIC COMMENT

1.   Any person or entity may appear in person or be represented by an authorized agent at any meeting of the
     Commission.

2.   Unless altered by the Chair, the order of the procedure on an application shall be:

     a. The supporting agency staff will introduce the application, including staff’s recommendations and a
        summary of pertinent written comments and reports concerning the application

     b. The applicant will be allowed up to 15 minutes to make their presentation.

     c. The Community Council representative can present their comments as applicable.

     d. Where applicable, persons in favor of, or not opposed to, the application will be invited to speak.

     e. Where applicable, persons opposing the application, in whole or in part will be invited to speak.

     f. Where applicable, the applicant will be allowed 5 minutes to provide concluding statements.

     g. Surrebutals may be allowed at the discretion of the Chair.

CONDUCT FOR APPLICANTS AND THE PUBLIC

1.   Speakers will be called to the podium by the Chair.

2.   Each speaker, before talking, shall give his or her name and address.

3.   All comments should be directed to the Commissioners, not to the staff or to members of the audience.

4.   For items where there are several people wishing to speak, the Chair may impose a time limit, usually 3
     minutes per person, or 5 minutes for a group spokesperson. If a time limit is imposed on any member or
     spokesperson of the public, then the same time limit is imposed on other members or spokespersons of the
     public, respectively.

5.   Unless otherwise allowed by the Chair, no questions shall be asked by the speaker or Commission Members.

6.   Only one speaker is permitted before the Commission at a time.

7.   The discussion must be confined to essential points stated in the application bearing on the desirability or
     undesirability of the application.

8.   The Chair may cease any presentation or information that has already been presented and acknowledge that it
     has been noted in the public record.

9.   No personal attacks shall be indulged in by either side, and such action shall be sufficient cause for stopping the
     speaker from proceeding.

10. No applause or public outbursts shall be permitted.

11. The Chair or supporting agency staff may request police support to remove offending individuals who refuse to
    abide by these rules.

12. After the public comment portion of a meeting or hearing has concluded, the discussion will be limited to the
    Planning Commission and Staff.

                                         PROJECT DESCRIPTION
The applicant, Steve Layton, is requesting Conditional Use approval for a warehouse/office use. The proposed
warehouse/office building is 479,083 square feet. This building will be on Lot #1 of the recently recorded 201
Logistics Center 4-lot Subdivision.

The parking lot shown on the site plan is quite extensive as the tenant for the building is a large multinational
delivery service company. As a result, the need for large truck parking and van parking is quite important.

The west and south sides of the warehouse building will have large semi-truck parking (236 stalls), and the north
side of the building will have van parking (210 stalls). Employee and visitor parking is located on the east side of
the building (551 stalls).

                                      PLANNING STAFF ANALYSIS
19.84.050 Approval/Denial Authority
The planning commission has the authority to approve, deny, or approve with conditions conditional use
applications.

   1. Planning Commission Approval.
          1. The planning commission shall review and approve or deny each application during a public
              meeting.
          2. The planning commission's decision shall be based on information presented through the public
              meeting process, including: the materials submitted by the applicant, the recommendation of the
              director or director's designee, and input from interested parties and affected entities.
          3. If conditions are specified, the director or director's designee shall issue a final approval letter upon
              satisfaction of the planning commission's conditions of approval.
          4. If the applicant fails to meet all conditions of approval within twelve months of the planning
              commission's decision, the application is deemed denied. A twelve-month extension may be
              granted upon the payment of an additional filing fee equal to the original filing fee.
          5. A planning commission decision shall be made on a complete conditional use application within a
              reasonable time frame, not to exceed ninety days. The planning commission is authorized to
              review and take action on an application as outlined in Section 19.84.040 after having notified the
              applicant of the meeting date.
          6. Failure by the applicant to provide information that has been requested by the planning
              commission, the director or director's designee to resolve conflicts with the standards in Section
              19.84.060 (above) may result in an application being denied.
   2. Decision. Each conditional use application shall be:
          1. Approved if the proposed use, including the manner and design in which a property is proposed
              for development, complies with the standards for approval outlined in Section 19.84.060; or
          2. Approved with conditions if the anticipated detrimental effects of the use, including the manner
              and design in which the property is proposed for development, can be mitigated with the
              imposition of reasonable conditions to bring about compliance with the standards outlined in
              Section 19.84.060; or
          3. Denied if the anticipated detrimental effects of the proposed use cannot be mitigated with the
              imposition of reasonable conditions of approval to bring about compliance with the standards
              outlined in Section 19.84.060.

                             PLANNING STAFF RECOMMENDATION
The MSD Planning Staff recommends that the Planning Commission grant Final Conditional Use Approval for a
Warehouse/Office use at 7777 West U201 Highway (Lot 1, 201 Logistics Center Subdivision), subject to the
following conditions:
            1. That the applicant shall comply with all MSD and Outside Agency Reviewer requirements and
                recommendations prior to final application approval.
            2. That all bonds for improvements and final fees related to the application be posted and/or paid
                prior to final approval.
            3. That the applicant be required to install a vinyl coated chain link fence along the north and east
                property lines.
            4. No signs are approved with this land use approval. Signs require separate land use applications,
                reviews, and approvals.
            5. Any modifications to these approved plans must be approved by the Magna Planning
                Commission, prior to any changes being implemented in the field.
            6. That a temporary construction trailer is allowed in combination with this project but must be
                removed within 30 days of approved final building permit inspection and/or a certificate of
                occupancy being issued.
            7. That the applicant follows the requirements and recommendations of the liquefaction analysis.
            8. That the applicant follows the recommendations of the geotechnical report.
            9. At the time of building permit application:
                    a. Footing and foundation excavations shall be inspected and approval in writing by a
                         Qualified Geotechnical Engineer prior to the placement of concrete forms or rebar.
                    b. Follow final grading and drainage plan approved during building review process.
                    c. Provide fire flow verification for the nearest fire hydrant and show how compliance is
                         going to be made with any Unified Fire District Guidelines.
            10. Fire department connection needs to be within 100 feet of fire hydrant on access road.
            11. Post indicator valve is required if not exterior door goes directly in Fire riser room.
            12. Fire Department connection (FDC) needs to be accessible on access road that is not on a dead-
                end road.
            13. Engineered building plans are required for the construction of the new building.

MSD Planning Staff Recommendation: Approval with conditions



                                          PROJECT DESCRIPTION
The applicant, Salt Lake County Parks and Recreation Department (Rep. Angelo Calacino) is requesting
Conditional Use approval of a canal trail. This will be a multipurpose trail for biking, walking and running.

The trail has been on the Salt Lake County Parks and Recreation’s Master Plan since the early 1990's and is one
of many north/south identified regional trails within Salt Lake County. Once completed, much like the Jordan
River Trail, it will be part of an overall countywide trail network allowing everyone pedestrian and bicycle access
to parks, schools, places of worship, shopping, entertainment centers, and places of work. Phase one was
constructed in 2008, and runs from 4130 W to 4800 W, Phase 2 was constructed in 2014, and runs from 4800 W
to 5600 W. Phase 3 was constructed in 2020, and runs from 5600 W to 7200 W, and intersects with the
Mountain View Corridor Trail.


                            SITE & VICINITY DESCRIPTION (see attached map)
 The Trail would run from 7200 West, along the current Utah and Salt Lake Canal, to 8000 West. The proposed
trail is approximately 5,600 linear feet in length.
         Request: Conditional Use                                         File #: CUP2021-000286


                                  GENERAL PLAN CONSIDERATIONS
The new Magna General Plan was adopted on March 23, 2021. As per Magna’s General Plan, when constructed,
the planned Utah and Salt Lake Canal and Bonneville Shoreline Trails will connect Magna Loop Trail alignment.
According to the Salt Lake County Regional Trail Master Plan, “The West Planning Area is the most underserved of
the five planning areas in terms of park land and recreational amenities. Working with Salt Lake County to identify
the proposed alignment of the proposed Magna Loop Trail is one of the General Plan’s strategy actions.



                         ISSUES OF CONCERN/PROPOSED MITIGATION
No issues of concern have been identified for the proposed application.


                                      NEIGHBORHOOD RESPONSE
Notices were sent to the property owners within 300’ of the subject property. No responses have been received
as of the writing of this report.

The Salt Lake County Parks and Rec. Dept. has sent out notice to neighboring property owners of the canal. They
have received calls regarding how the trail might impact the privacy in the backyards of the homes it passes by.

Most property owners have embraced the trail, residents living along the trail want to add gates in their fences
once the trail is completed so they can have direct access.

The once littered and weed and rodent invested canal bank is now clean, maintained and a function asset to the
community.


                                       PLANNING STAFF ANALYSIS
19.84.050 Approval/Denial Authority
The planning commission has the authority to approve, deny, or approve with conditions conditional use
applications.

    1. Planning Commission Approval.
           1. The planning commission shall review and approve or deny each application during a public
              meeting.
           2. The planning commission's decision shall be based on information presented through the public
              meeting process, including: the materials submitted by the applicant, the recommendation of the
              director or director's designee, and input from interested parties and affected entities.
           3. If conditions are specified, the director or director's designee shall issue a final approval letter upon
              satisfaction of the planning commission's conditions of approval.
           4. If the applicant fails to meet all conditions of approval within twelve months of the planning
              commission's decision, the application is deemed denied. A twelve-month extension may be
              granted upon the payment of an additional filing fee equal to the original filing fee.
           5. A planning commission decision shall be made on a complete conditional use application within a
              reasonable time frame, not to exceed ninety days. The planning commission is authorized to


Rezone                                                                                                      Page 2 of 3
         Request: Conditional Use                                      File #: CUP2021-000286

               review and take action on an application as outlined in Section 19.84.040 after having notified the
               applicant of the meeting date.
           6. Failure by the applicant to provide information that has been requested by the planning
               commission, the director or director's designee to resolve conflicts with the standards in Section
               19.84.060 (above) may result in an application being denied.
    2. Decision. Each conditional use application shall be:
           1. Approved if the proposed use, including the manner and design in which a property is proposed
               for development, complies with the standards for approval outlined in Section 19.84.060; or
           2. Approved with conditions if the anticipated detrimental effects of the use, including the manner
               and design in which the property is proposed for development, can be mitigated with the
               imposition of reasonable conditions to bring about compliance with the standards outlined in
               Section 19.84.060; or
           3. Denied if the anticipated detrimental effects of the proposed use cannot be mitigated with the
               imposition of reasonable conditions of approval to bring about compliance with the standards
               outlined in Section 19.84.060.

HISTORY
Adopted by Ord. 17-01-03 on 1/17/2017

                              PLANNING STAFF RECOMMENDATION
The MSD Planning Staff recommends that the Magna Planning Commission approve the Conditional Use for a
Canal Trail at 7200 West until approximately 7988 West Molly Drive (east of 8000 West), subject to the
following conditions:
       1. That the applicant complies with all Agency Reviewer recommendations and requirements prior to
            final land use approval.
       2. That the hours of operation will be consistent with other trails and parks in the area, being limited
            to the hours within dusk and dawn.
       3. That the applicant works with the MSD Planning Staff on the signage package for the trail.

                                          Case# CUP2021-000306


           Conditional Use Summary and Recommendation
Public Body: Magna Planning Commission
Meeting Date: June 10, 2021
Parcel ID: 14-29-103-003-0000 & 14-29-103-004-0000
Current Zone: C-2 (Commercial)
Property Address: 8609 West Magna Main Street
Request: Conditional Use approval for a new fire station
Applicant Name: Unified Fire Department (Rep Steve Simmons)

MSD Planner: Diana Martinez
MSD Planning Staff Recommendation: Approval with conditions




                                          PROJECT DESCRIPTION
The applicant, Unified Fire Department (rep Steve Simmons), is requesting approval for a new fire station to be
built at 8609 West Magna Main Street. The proposed fire station will replace the previous fire station building
at this location.

The layout of the building will be similar to the existing fire station. The station building will sit along Magna
Main Street and the parking will still be beyond the building at the south end of the property.


                            SITE & VICINITY DESCRIPTION (see attached map)
The subject property is along the easterly end of Magna Main Street and located within the C-2/zc zone. There
are a few parcels in this small section of Magna Main that are zoned R-2-6.5. The parcels to the direct east, and
across Buccaneer Drive are zoned Commercial C-2.
         Request: Conditional Use                                        File #: CUP2021-000306




                                    GENERAL PLAN CONSIDERATIONS
The new Magna General Plan was adopted on March 23, 2021. As per Magna’s General Plan, the subject
properties are located where there should be encouragement of development and redevelopment along Magna
Main Street to strengthen its role as a historical center and urban district. Adopting zoning that addresses
building form, setbacks, parking, landscaping, block structure, uses, and other components with Main Street to
encourage appropriate redevelopment/development patterns to protect the historic character of Main Street
while protecting property rights to encourage economic development.

                         ISSUES OF CONCERN/PROPOSED MITIGATION
No issues of concern have been identified for the proposed rezone.

The applicant will be required to combine the two parcels that the existing building now sits on. It is not
acceptable for new development to span over two different parcels.


                                      NEIGHBORHOOD RESPONSE
Notices were sent to the property owners within 300’ of the subject property. No responses have been received
as of the writing of this report.

                                      PLANNING STAFF ANALYSIS
19.84.050 Approval/Denial Authority
The planning commission has the authority to approve, deny, or approve with conditions conditional use
applications.

   1. Planning Commission Approval.
          1. The planning commission shall review and approve or deny each application during a public
              meeting.
          2. The planning commission's decision shall be based on information presented through the public
              meeting process, including: the materials submitted by the applicant, the recommendation of the
              director or director's designee, and input from interested parties and affected entities.
          3. If conditions are specified, the director or director's designee shall issue a final approval letter upon
              satisfaction of the planning commission's conditions of approval.
          4. If the applicant fails to meet all conditions of approval within twelve months of the planning
              commission's decision, the application is deemed denied. A twelve-month extension may be
              granted upon the payment of an additional filing fee equal to the original filing fee.
          5. A planning commission decision shall be made on a complete conditional use application within a
              reasonable time frame, not to exceed ninety days. The planning commission is authorized to
              review and take action on an application as outlined in Section 19.84.040 after having notified the
              applicant of the meeting date.
          6. Failure by the applicant to provide information that has been requested by the planning
              commission, the director or director's designee to resolve conflicts with the standards in Section
              19.84.060 (above) may result in an application being denied.
   2. Decision. Each conditional use application shall be:
          1. Approved if the proposed use, including the manner and design in which a property is proposed
              for development, complies with the standards for approval outlined in Section 19.84.060; or
          2. Approved with conditions if the anticipated detrimental effects of the use, including the manner
              and design in which the property is proposed for development, can be mitigated with the
              imposition of reasonable conditions to bring about compliance with the standards outlined in
              Section 19.84.060; or
          3. Denied if the anticipated detrimental effects of the proposed use cannot be mitigated with the
              imposition of reasonable conditions of approval to bring about compliance with the standards
              outlined in Section 19.84.060.

                              PLANNING STAFF RECOMMENDATION
The MSD Planning Staff recommends that the Magna Planning Commission approve the Conditional Use for a
Fire Station at 8609 W. Magna Main Street, subject to the following conditions:
        1. That the applicant complies with all Agency Reviewer recommendations and requirements prior to
            final land use approval.
        2. That the applicant obtains a building permit for the construction of the fire station building.

         3. That the applicant combines the two parcels (14-29-103-003-0000 & 14-29-103-004-0000) into one
            parcel.
         4. That the applicant submits a Landscape Plan to staff, showing the upgraded landscaping within the
            10-foot landscape buffer on the west side of the building. (Landscaping plans must be stamped by
            a certified landscape architect.)
         5. That the applicant must submit water and sewer availability letters for the Health Department
            approval.

                                          Case# CUP2021-000321


           Conditional Use Summary and Recommendation
Public Body: Magna Planning Commission
Meeting Date: June 10, 2021
Parcel ID: 14-21-479-013-0000
Current Zone: C-3/zc (Commercial with zoning conditions -Used Auto Sales only)
Property Address: 2646 South 7200 West
Request: Conditional Use approval for a 3,200 square foot accessory carport building
Applicant Name: Jose’ Rodriquez

MSD Planner: Diana Martinez
MSD Planning Staff Recommendation: Approval with conditions


                                          PROJECT DESCRIPTION
The applicant, Jose’ Rodriquez, would like to put a 3,200 square foot accessory carport in the north area of his
used car lot, in order to store equipment used for the car lot. The carport will have a roof and two sides but will
not be entirely enclosed.

The carport building would be located in the northwest end of the property. The closest residence to this
structure would be about 90 feet. The entire car lot is fenced.

The car lot received final conditional use approval February 17, 2021.



                            SITE & VICINITY DESCRIPTION (see attached map)
The property is located on 7200 West immediately South of the Entheos Academy School and abuts a residential
subdivision to the West. To the east across 7200 West are residential homes located in West Valley City.


                         ISSUES OF CONCERN/PROPOSED MITIGATION
No issues of concern have been identified for this application. As noted above, the closest residential dwelling to
this structure will be over 90 feet.

All agency reviewers have given a conceptual ok for the project.
         Request: Conditional Use                                        File #: CUP2021-000321




                                     NEIGHBORHOOD RESPONSE
Notices were sent to the property owners within 300’ of the subject property. No responses have been received
as of the writing of this report.


                                      PLANNING STAFF ANALYSIS
19.84.050 Approval/Denial Authority
The planning commission has the authority to approve, deny, or approve with conditions conditional use
applications.

   1. Planning Commission Approval.
          1. The planning commission shall review and approve or deny each application during a public
              meeting.
          2. The planning commission's decision shall be based on information presented through the public
              meeting process, including: the materials submitted by the applicant, the recommendation of the
              director or director's designee, and input from interested parties and affected entities.
          3. If conditions are specified, the director or director's designee shall issue a final approval letter upon
              satisfaction of the planning commission's conditions of approval.
          4. If the applicant fails to meet all conditions of approval within twelve months of the planning
              commission's decision, the application is deemed denied. A twelve-month extension may be
              granted upon the payment of an additional filing fee equal to the original filing fee.
          5. A planning commission decision shall be made on a complete conditional use application within a
              reasonable time frame, not to exceed ninety days. The planning commission is authorized to
              review and take action on an application as outlined in Section 19.84.040 after having notified the
              applicant of the meeting date.
          6. Failure by the applicant to provide information that has been requested by the planning
              commission, the director or director's designee to resolve conflicts with the standards in Section
              19.84.060 (above) may result in an application being denied.
   2. Decision. Each conditional use application shall be:
          1. Approved if the proposed use, including the manner and design in which a property is proposed
              for development, complies with the standards for approval outlined in Section 19.84.060; or
          2. Approved with conditions if the anticipated detrimental effects of the use, including the manner
              and design in which the property is proposed for development, can be mitigated with the
              imposition of reasonable conditions to bring about compliance with the standards outlined in
              Section 19.84.060; or
          3. Denied if the anticipated detrimental effects of the proposed use cannot be mitigated with the
              imposition of reasonable conditions of approval to bring about compliance with the standards
              outlined in Section 19.84.060.

                                       PROJECT DESCRIPTION
        On June 11, 2015, the applicant’s partner, Scott Gailey, acted as the applicant for a Planned Unit
Development (PUD) subdivision (Magna Hamptons) for 80 two-family dwelling units. The project was approved
with the assumption that the applicant would be acquiring the two additional parcels to the south which
connected to Parkway Boulevard (2820 South).
        The applicant, Dee Bates, has not been able to acquire those two parcels to the south (2710 South 7200
West and 2802 South 7200 West). As a result, the applicant has decided to come back to the Planning
Commission to ask for approval to amend the PUD. This includes reconfiguring the remaining available land to
include a second access point for ingress/egress to the subdivision and adding ten additional lots.
        Increasing the entire PUD density by ten units would allow for a density of 8.8 units per acre on the
7.51-acre site. The original conditional use approval limited the maximum units per acre to eight (8).
        The proposed configuration of the property includes the roadway going straight out to 7200 West,
rather than going south and connecting to Parkway Blvd (2820 South) as previously designed. Therefore, the
PUD’s roadway would be a horseshoe shaped drive with both entrances from 7200 West. Please see attached
PUD plat.

The property is located on 7200 West immediately South of the Copperview Village Condominiums.

To the East across 7200 West are residential homes located in West Valley City.


                         ISSUES OF CONCERN/PROPOSED MITIGATION
No issues of concern have been identified for this application.

Applicant will be required to fence along the perimeter of the project and fence all private yards.

The proposed PUD plat meets the requirements of the Recreation Facility and Open Space Standards. With the
current proposal the entire Magna Hamptons PUD will have 40% open space, and the correct number of
recreation facilities required.

The current recreation facilities include a 14,000 square foot sports field, a children’s playground, two gazebos,
and two barbeque areas.

as of the writing of this report.



                                       PLANNING STAFF ANALYSIS
19.84.050 Approval/Denial Authority
The planning commission has the authority to approve, deny, or approve with conditions conditional use
applications.

    1. Planning Commission Approval.
           1. The planning commission shall review and approve or deny each application during a public
              meeting.
           2. The planning commission's decision shall be based on information presented through the public
              meeting process, including: the materials submitted by the applicant, the recommendation of the
              director or director's designee, and input from interested parties and affected entities.
           3. If conditions are specified, the director or director's designee shall issue a final approval letter upon
              satisfaction of the planning commission's conditions of approval.
           4. If the applicant fails to meet all conditions of approval within twelve months of the planning
              commission's decision, the application is deemed denied. A twelve-month extension may be
              granted upon the payment of an additional filing fee equal to the original filing fee.
           5. A planning commission decision shall be made on a complete conditional use application within a
              reasonable time frame, not to exceed ninety days. The planning commission is authorized to


Rezone                                                                                                      Page 2 of 3
         Request: Amended Subdivision Plat                                 File #: PAM2021-000298

               review and take action on an application as outlined in Section 19.84.040 after having notified the
               applicant of the meeting date.
           6. Failure by the applicant to provide information that has been requested by the planning
               commission, the director or director's designee to resolve conflicts with the standards in Section
               19.84.060 (above) may result in an application being denied.
    2. Decision. Each conditional use application shall be:
           1. Approved if the proposed use, including the manner and design in which a property is proposed
               for development, complies with the standards for approval outlined in Section 19.84.060; or
           2. Approved with conditions if the anticipated detrimental effects of the use, including the manner
               and design in which the property is proposed for development, can be mitigated with the
               imposition of reasonable conditions to bring about compliance with the standards outlined in
               Section 19.84.060; or
           3. Denied if the anticipated detrimental effects of the proposed use cannot be mitigated with the
               imposition of reasonable conditions of approval to bring about compliance with the standards
               outlined in Section 19.84.060.

19.78.110 Amendments To The Development Plan
The division director or designee may authorize minor changes in the location, siting, or character of buildings and
structures if required to resolve an engineering or other technical issue, or other circumstances not identified at
the time the final development plan was approved. No change authorized under this section may cause any of the
following ("major changes"):

    1.    A change in the use and/or character of the development.
    2.    An increase in the overall density and/or intensity of use.
    3.    An increase of more than five percent in overall coverage of structures.
    4.    A reduction or change in character of approved open space.
    5.    A reduction of required off-street parking by more than five percent.
    6.    A detrimental alteration to the pedestrian, vehicular, bicycle, circulation, or utility networks.
    7.    A reduction in required street pavement widths.
    8.    An increase in building height.
    9.    A decrease in building setback.

Any major changes must be proposed to the planning commission after receipt of a recommendation by planning
staff. Proposals under numbers 1. through 9. above require the filing of a new application. Generally speaking, any
major changes must be recorded as amendments in accordance with the procedure established for adopting the
final development plan.

                              PLANNING STAFF RECOMMENDATION
The MSD Planning Staff recommends that the Magna Planning Commission approve the request to amend the
Conditional Use and PUD Subdivision (Magna Hamptons) allowing for a density of up to 9 units per acre by
allowing for Phase #3 to have ten additional lots, subject to the following conditions:
        1. That the applicant be required to and comply with the recommendations from all reviewing
            agencies.
        2. That the applicant be required to install a 6’ high solid visual barrier wood, masonry or other
            material designated by the Planning Commission, along the property line around the residential
            dwelling units.
        3. All individual private yards be fenced entirely for privacy.
        4. That the applicant complies with the Development Standards for Recreation Facilities and Open
            Space for the PUD project.
        5. That the applicant be required to submit a Final Landscape Plan for the proposed new lots to staff
            for approval.
        6. That the applicant be required to comply with the parking requirements for guest parking.
        7. That the applicant be required to meet all County Engineering Standards for the private roadway
            within the project.
        8. That the HOA Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions (CCR’s), note that there is to be no on-street
            parking for residents or guests, and that signage to reflect “No Parking” be put along the roadways.
            Applicant should submit a copy of the CCR’s to Planning Staff.
